stableFactsAndClaims: There are forty puzzles; twenty-six checked, fourteen unchecked on the lower shelf with yellow bands; not all forty are ready to borrow.
Eighteen checked puzzles are complete; eight lack one to five pieces.
Lending incomplete puzzles with labels is the volunteer group's suggestion, unapproved by the manager; borrowers should decide whether missing pieces matter.
Some titles are tiny and three boxes lack finished-puzzle pictures; larger labels and photos are uncosted, with no agreed person to create or maintain them despite an available camera.
Staff propose the existing board-game system: fourteen-day loans and one renewal if unreserved.
The system records missing-piece notes but not photographs, which must remain with physical boxes.
The immediate request is permission to finish checking fourteen puzzles and test loans with two complete puzzles to observe returns.
The small test does not settle incomplete-puzzle lending; comments go to the circulation supervisor by Wednesday for Friday manager review.

ambiguity: Incomplete-puzzle lending, labeling and photographs, and use of the loan system remain proposed rather than approved.
